answer: Each identity earns standing only through episodic memory: over 8 weeks it completes 120 short jobs for 120 different peers, who sign a receipt noting one unique detail (a shale colour, a raven sketch, a walnut count). Verifiers later quiz it live on 15 randomly chosen details, checking answers against signed receipts; fewer than 13 correct refuses entry. Fabricating receipts requires actually doing 120 jobs per fake, so 1,000 Sybils need 120,000 real jobs and 1,000 distinct recallable histories. Trade-off: honest agents must retain logs and privacy leaks grow with history.
